No.

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
speechtext: May I make a suggestion here for consideration. I think an important point has been made by various members. If there is no controversy with regard to clauses 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 we might pass those tonight and stand clause 4. Overnight let the drafters get busy and produce, as they always have in the past, a solution to this problem.

speakerposition: Secretary of State of Canada; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Liberal Party House Leader
speechtext: I think that is an admirable suggestion.
I have an amendment I want to move to clause 5. If you are going to stand clause 4 you might as well stand clause 5.

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
speechtext: Is it agreed that the committee shall stand clauses 4 and 5?

Agreed.
Clauses 4 and 5 stand.
On clause 6.
I should like to have a definition of a "farm wagon".
Mr. Chairman, it is now ten minutes to eleven and a number of matters remain to be dealt with. I think we should call it 10.30 as agreed.

speakerposition: Secretary of State of Canada; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Liberal Party House Leader
speechtext:
I think it seems pretty evident that we have made a fair amount of progress and there does not seem to be much prospect of making any more, so I move that the committee rise, report progress and ask leave to sit again on another day.
Clause 6 stands.
Progress reported.

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
speechtext: Would the leader of the house outline the business for tomorrow?

speakerposition: Secretary of State of Canada; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Liberal Party House Leader
speechtext:
Before doing that I should like to express genuine appreciation for the co-operation which hon. members have given on a day when, perhaps, co-operation was not as easy as it might have been on some other days when it was a little cooler.
Tomorrow, as I indicated earlier in the day, the government would like to take the supplementary estimate which was tabled today, unless there is any objection to doing so, with a view to adding it so that it might be included in the interim supply to be considered next week. Then we will go on with the estimates of the Department of Transport.
I am advised that there is agreement among all parties that I can make a motion
to refer the report of the chief electoral officer to the committee on privileges and elections at the beginning of proceedings tomorrow and that there would be no debate. If that understanding is correct, I appreciate it very much and will be glad to do this.

speakerposition: Official Opposition House Leader; Progressive Conservative Party House Leader
speechtext: That is agreeable as far as we are concerned.
That is agreeable to us.

speakerposition: N.D.P. House Leader; Whip of the N.D.P.
speechtext: The same with us.

speakerposition: Secretary of State of Canada; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Liberal Party House Leader
speechtext: Then, on Monday, I am advised there is general agreement on all sides of the house that if the government will put on the order paper the motion regarding the remuneration and pensions of members of parliament there would be no objection raised to going ahead with all stages except third reading on Monday. The third reading would be held over until the next day.
Hear, hear.

speakerposition: Secretary of State of Canada; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Liberal Party House Leader
speechtext:
If that correctly represents the sense of the house, and it can be so ordered, I will undertake that notice of the resolution will be given tomorrow evening so that it will appear in Votes and Proceedings. That provides the 48 hours' notice required by the rules. I have not sought unanimous consent for this, but I intend, also, to put in a notice respecting the Judges Act and I would hope it may receive similar treatment. I am not asking that this be done, but I would just hope it would be the case.
After those two matters have been dealt with on Monday, if there should be any time left, I know the Minister of Finance would like to complete this bill. We have made very good progress on it this evening. Then, perhaps, we could consider which of two other measures we might take, whether the surcharge legislation or the measure dealing with the economic council. I would consult with hon. gentlemen opposite if there were need for anything further to be added.
